---
title: "Comparative Analysis of Modern Lossy Image Formats for the Web"
subtitle: "An Empirical Evaluation of JPEG, WebP, AVIF, and JPEG XL"
abstract: |
  Modern web applications increasingly rely on efficient image compression to
  balance visual quality and bandwidth. This paper presents a systematic
  empirical comparison of four lossy image formats — JPEG, WebP, AVIF, and
  JPEG XL — using perceptual quality metrics (SSIMULACRA2, Butteraugli) alongside
  traditional metrics (PSNR, SSIM). We first determine optimal encoder parameters
  for each format through parameter sweep studies, then compare the formats at
  their best operating points. Our analysis reveals that both AVIF and JPEG XL
  significantly outperform JPEG and WebP in compression efficiency. While
  SSIMULACRA2 scores show parity between AVIF and JPEG XL, Butteraugli
  consistently favors JPEG XL. Combined with JPEG XL's substantially lower
  encoding time, our findings support the adoption of JPEG XL for web image
  delivery. We complement the quantitative analysis with a qualitative
  examination of compression artifacts, observing that AVIF tends to preserve
  sharp details at the expense of textures, whereas JPEG XL maintains a more
  balanced reproduction.
keywords:
  - image compression
  - AVIF
  - JPEG XL
  - WebP
  - SSIMULACRA2
  - Butteraugli
  - perceptual quality
  - web performance
---
